A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CREPE research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across additions, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original CREPE experiments on molecular tempering, ImageNet generation, maze trajectory stitching and MNIST, including Tables 1–3 and appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original sentiment-controlled text-generation results and a Gaussian-mixture sampling study.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the annealing paths, Radon–Nikodym-based swap acceptance and optional local exploration are retained. Applying the existing discrete-diffusion procedure to text introduces no new CREPE component.

E1.justification: V2 adds SST-2-based positive/negative sentiment-controlled text generation and a synthetic one-dimensional Gaussian-mixture reward-tilting task. These substantially extend coverage beyond the retained molecular, ImageNet, maze and MNIST experiments.

E2.justification: The retained experiments preserve their FKC, RNE, CompDiffuser and CFG/SMC comparisons. The new text experiment extends the CFG/SMC comparator set already used for MNIST; the mixture study varies SMC batch sizes without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: B.6 introduces a text protocol with target/proposal CFG-strength sweeps, 100 diffusion steps, 1,000 length-1,024 samples, 150 CREPE burn-in steps, and perplexity/sentiment metrics. The mixture study uses 150,000 samples and SMC batch sizes 4/10/100. Existing protocols in B.1–B.5 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New A.1 tests whether aggregating small SMC batches preserves target mode weights. Figure 3 adds molecular marginal-distribution diagnostics, while the text strength sweeps and Appendix D traces examine sensitivity, convergence and an accuracy failure.

E5.justification: Molecular error bars still use three repetitions of metric subsampling, and image reward plots retain mean/std reporting across five prompts. The additions introduce no seed reporting, independent-run uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original figure results are unchanged. New text results report up to roughly fivefold lower perplexity than SMC at target strength 1.8, with an accuracy failure at target/proposal strengths 1.4/1.0. New mixture and molecular histograms also report closer distributional agreement for CREPE.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, acceptance-rate derivations, discretisation formulas and computational-cost argument are retained. A backward-process arrow is corrected in Section 2.3, but this is a notation correction. The mini-batch discussion adds empirical illustration and informal reasoning, not a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and central conclusion retain the same claims about pretrained-model control, sequential sampling, diversity, online refinement and competitiveness with SMC. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 explains why repeated mini-batch SMC can recover diversity while distorting mode weights, and tentatively attributes text instability to propagation of an accepted poor sample. Existing burn-in and approximation-error limitations are moved from A.7 into the conclusion rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: V2 adds code/project links and text implementation details: SEDD-Medium fine-tuning for five epochs, GPT2-XL with LoRA for perplexity, and a linked DistilBERT evaluator. A.3 also newly clarifies shared proposals with RNE-based SMC; this documents comparison settings without establishing a procedural change.

R1.justification: V2 adds Amini et al. for the text setup and four references supporting future annealing/path-selection work. It expands attribution of proposal choices and discussion of mini-batch SMC, while retaining CREPE's central positioning as a parallel-tempering alternative to SMC.

P1.justification: Changes are targeted: new appendix subsections, relocation of limitations into Section 5, a future-work extension, an LLM-use disclosure and conference-header updates. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Four new multipanel figures add molecular histograms, text comparison curves, the mixture study and text iteration traces. The existing TICA scatter plot is relocated and subsequent figures are renumbered. Original figures and all three tables are retained, with some resizing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: Quantitative text tests strengthen v1's largely qualitative discrete-diffusion evidence, and the mini-batch study clarifies bias versus diversity. Added access links and discussion of the text failure improve transparency. These gains are tempered by missing uncertainty estimates for the additions and an unexplained mismatch between B.6's 1,150 total CREPE steps and Figure 17's traces extending beyond 2,000 sample indices.
